Racial demographics of the force

Project 57 · a folder, templates-demographics/, one file per group · index · repo randomcase/racial-demographics-of-the-force

The record — the Defense Casualty Analysis System — kept race in five categories under the terms of its day, and did not keep a Hispanic category at all. The folder keeps one file per category under the record’s own term, with the population share for comparison, and says where an estimate is an estimate. Requested for the Johnson page (project 42), whose years are the years the disproportion was largest.

US figures are the Defense Casualty Analysis System by year of death; the last column is the range in project 55. Every Vietnam page carries this box.

GroupRecord termPopulation 1970DeathsShare of deathsNote
WhiteCaucasian87.5%50,12086.1%About 86% of deaths against 87–88% of the population: the majority, in proportion.
BlackNegro11.1%7,24312.4%About 12.4% of deaths against 11% of the population over the whole war; but in 1965–1966 Black soldiers were roughly a fifth of Army combat deaths, and the Pentagon changed assignment patterns in 1967 to bring the share down. Project 100,000 (1966–1971) took 354,000 men below the normal standards, 41% of them Black, mostly into the infantry. In 1967 a draft-board study found 64% of eligible Black men were drafted against 31% of eligible whites, largely because of deferments the others could reach. Black officers were about 2% of the Army officer corps in 1968.
Hispanicnot recorded separately; counted as Caucasian4.5%3,0705.3%The record did not keep a Hispanic category, so the count is an estimate (about 3,000–3,500, or 5–6% of deaths, against about 4.5% of the population). Ralph Guzmán’s 1969 study of the Southwest found Spanish-surnamed men were 19% of the region’s casualties and about 12% of its population.
American IndianAmerican Indian0.4%2260.4%About 42,000 served, 90% of them volunteers; 226 killed, about 0.4% of deaths against 0.4% of the population, one of the highest service rates of any group.
Asian and Pacific IslanderMongoloid (116) and Malayan (252)0.7%3680.6%The record’s two categories, kept here under the terms it used; 368 killed, about 0.6% of deaths against about 0.7% of the population.
